Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — PrivateLink vs VPC peering (tech details)

Hi Jordan / Alex —

Thanks for sharing the diagram. Short answers up top, followed by specifics:

Recommendation summary:
- PrivateLink (AWS) / Private Service Connect (GCP): Recommended for most customers who want a simple, secure integration without making wide route-table changes. Provides an interface endpoint per VPC/account and keeps traffic on the AWS network. Good for strict egress/ingress controls and compliance.
- VPC Peering / VPC Network Peering: Can provide slightly lower latency and higher throughput for heavy sustained traffic but requires configuring route tables and potentially cross-account peering. More operational work and firewall changes.

We support both in AWS and have a Private Service Connect option for GCP. If your primary concern is minimizing operational blast radius and keeping control-plane calls private, PrivateLink is the usual starting point. If you expect sustained high throughput (large model serving across many instances) and want minimal per-request overhead, peering can be considered.

Required/network checklist (example values — we will tailor to your CIDRs):
- Control-plane endpoint: TCP 443 to our control-plane interface endpoint (PrivateLink) or to managed IP ranges if peering.
- Example allowlist entries (you can paste these to infra):
  - redwood-controlplane-us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com (PrivateLink interface endpoint per-account)
  - 52.204.12.0/24 (example egress IP block — final will be a short list we provide before cutover)
  - If using peering: allow all traffic between your VPC CIDR (e.g., 10.0.0.0/16) and our service VPC CIDR in the peering connection.
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS) for control plane + 443 for model serving endpoints. If you plan to push artifacts to S3, ensure outbound HTTPS to your S3 endpoints or a VPC endpoint for S3.
- DNS: For PrivateLink, we can optionally provide private DNS names that resolve to the interface endpoints in your account. This avoids changes to client configs.

KMS & Compliance notes (Vivek) — high level:
- We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS and have options for HSM-backed keys for Private deployments.}
  - For Hosted/Dedicated, we can integrate with your KMS using cross-account key policies or grant access via a service-backed key.
  - For Private deployments (when workloads live in your VPC), keys remain in your account and control.
- SOC 2: we can provide our SOC 2 Type II report and an evidence checklist. For Private VPC deployments, we will include a short attestation on network isolation and key handling.

Attachments: redwood_private_vpc_networking_guide.pdf (contains step-by-step PrivateLink setup, sample CloudFormation, and example allowlist templates).

Next steps:
1) If you want to proceed with PrivateLink, Alex — can you confirm your VPC CIDR and whether you're doing cross-account interface endpoints?
2) We'll schedule a 30-min technical sync (Sean + Vivek + your infra) — propose Wednesday 8/11 at 11:00 AM PT.

Happy to adjust based on your timeline.

- Sean
